# Codemap — issue 0147, the Uprising points-limit gap

Every file the issue has to change, one line each. The issue's only acceptance criterion is the scenario `docs/testing/at-least-roster-points-limit`, so the whole map belongs to the single increment `uprising-points-limit`. Scope is fenced by the issue: only `src/evaluator/` and its unit tests may change, and nothing under `docs/testing/` may be touched at all.

The map is a first cut from search, not from a diagnosis — the report's three complaints (occupied slot `current` 0, no message for limit `00f6-c1b3-ee85-5c02`, the budget-versus-sum reading) meet the engine in these modules, and the researcher narrows it.

- `src/evaluator/constraints.js` — Evaluates a limit at an anchor against the counted frame, including `scope="force"`; the report carries no result at all for `00f6-c1b3-ee85-5c02`, and a missing result is the direct cause of both the absent violation and the slot's `current` 0.
- `src/evaluator/report.js` — Projects a slot's `current`, `effectiveMin`, `effectiveMax`, `headroom` and `isBlocked` out of the constraint results, falling back to 0 where no result exists; the manifest asserts exactly these fields on the occupied Uprising slot.
- `src/evaluator/evalTree.js` — Joins the roster's selections onto the resolved definitions and decides which anchors exist and under which frame; the Uprising selection sits two levels down, below a group and below a `hidden="true"` parent entry, and it has to end up as a counted anchor of the force.
- `src/evaluator/offer.js` — Builds the offered slots below a carrier and carries the visibility gates of the groups it descends through; the occupied Uprising slot has to be addressable as `defId 4bc4-8781-2091-d9df` with `anchorKind occupied`.
- `src/evaluator/countIndex.js` — Holds the scope-keyed counts a `field="selections"`, `scope="force"` query reads; the manifest's constant `actual` 1 comes from here.
- `src/evaluator/modifiers.js` — Applies a `set` whose `field` is a constraint id, gated by an `and` group of two conditions on the same cost limit; roster 01 needs that `set` to raise the bound from 0 to 1 and rosters 02/03 need it to stay off.
- `src/evaluator/query.js` — Resolves a `limit::<costTypeId>` field, which it takes from the roster budget rather than the count index, and settles the `atLeast` comparison at the threshold itself; roster 03 turns on this reading.
- `src/evaluator/rosterBudget.js` — Owns the roster's configured cost limit and the roster-wide `budget::<costTypeId>` rule; roster 03 asserts that rule firing with actual 2000 against bound 1999 while the configured limit stays 1999.
- `src/evaluator/effectiveState.js` — Derives an anchor's effective base state, `hidden` inheritance among it; the carrier's chain is `hidden="true"` entry → visible group → `hidden="true"` entry, and this module decides whether that chain suppresses anything the manifest asserts.

Read-only for this issue, never edited: `docs/testing/at-least-roster-points-limit/scenario.json`, its `rosters/*.ros` and its `README.md` are the specification, and `src/evaluator/e2e.testcatalog.test.js` is the manifest-driven runner that reads them.

increments.title: The Uprising points-limit gate reports what the catalog data demands
increments.goal: All three rosters of the pinned scenario `docs/testing/at-least-roster-points-limit` match their manifest expectations: the single Uprising selection is counted in its force, its force-scoped `max 0` limit produces a result, the gated `set` raises that bound only at a configured budget of 2000, and `limit::<costTypeId>` reads the roster's configured cost limit instead of the summed cost of its selections.
criteria: `npx vitest run src/evaluator` exits 0, with the three previously failing cases `Szenario: at-least-roster-points-limit > rosters/01-limit-2000-gate-open.ros`, `> rosters/02-limit-1999-gate-closed.ros` and `> rosters/03-limit-1999-spent-2000-gate-closed.ros` green.

Roster 01 (`costLimit` 2000, 0 spent): no violation is reported for `00f6-c1b3-ee85-5c02` and none for `budget::ecfa-8486-4f6c-c249`; the occupied slot `4bc4-8781-2091-d9df` reports `current` 1, `effectiveMin` null, `effectiveMax` 1, `headroom` 0 and `isMandatoryUnmet` false.

Roster 02 (`costLimit` 1999, 0 spent): `00f6-c1b3-ee85-5c02` fires with `actual` 1 against `bound` 0, and the occupied slot `4bc4-8781-2091-d9df` reports `current` 1, `effectiveMin` null, `effectiveMax` 0 and `isBlocked` true.

Roster 03 (`costLimit` 1999, 2000 spent): the gate stays closed exactly as in roster 02 — `00f6-c1b3-ee85-5c02` fires `actual` 1 / `bound` 0 — and `budget::ecfa-8486-4f6c-c249` fires `actual` 2000 / `bound` 1999, so the configured limit and the spent sum are demonstrably two different quantities.
No file under `docs/testing/` is added, changed or deleted, and no file outside `src/evaluator/` is changed.
Every other case of `npx vitest run src/evaluator` that passed before still passes: no scenario, unit or cross-catalog test regresses.

return.plan:
## What is wrong

One defect, in one function, explains all three failing cases. The Uprising limit `00f6-c1b3-ee85-5c02` is `type="max" value="0" field="selections" scope="force" shared="true" includeChildSelections="false"` and sits on the entry `4bc4-8781-2091-d9df`. That entry's selection sits one selection level below the force: force `2bfa-e64a-7123-895f` -> selection `6fcf-b33d-3cf5-b56a` ("Army composition rules") -> selection `4bc4-8781-2091-d9df`.

`countIndex.js` books every contribution into one of four buckets per scope key, chosen by the boundaries the contribution crosses on its way up to the frame. For the force frame, the strictly intervening node `6fcf-...` is a non-force node, so the Uprising contribution lands in the SELECTION bucket, not BASE. `buildIndex(...).get(key, includeChildSelections=false, ...)` sums BASE only -> `selectionCount` 0.

`constraints.js` `countingFlagsOf(limit, node)` (lines 83-90) already knows this reading is wrong for a shared, entry-anchored limit: `includeChildSelections="false"` means "just scope's field", not "nothing" (`docs/battlescribe-data-format.md` §7.6, attribute table: "`false` zaehlt *just `scope`'s `field`* — also eingeschraenkt, **nicht** leer"). It therefore raises `includeChildSelections` to `true` before the query — but only for `limit.scope === ScopeKeyword.ROSTER` (Issue 083). The same argument holds verbatim for `scope="force"`: §7.6 states the rule scope-generically, and the sibling attribute row makes the force frame explicit in the other direction ("`includeChildForces` ... `false` rechnet *only from parent force selections* — die Auswahlen des eigenen Kontingents zaehlen also weiter mit"). The selections of the own force are all its selections, nested ones included. Restricting the raise to `roster` was an under-application, and this scenario is the case that exposes it.

## Verified consequences of the defect (measured, not guessed)

I ran the engine facade on the three pinned rosters with a throwaway script (never committed). Everything else in this scenario already works:

- Roster 01 (`costLimit` 2000): the `and` gate opens at the threshold itself, the `set 1` on the constraint id lands — the slot reports `effectiveMax` 1. `atLeast` is already inclusive. Only `current` is 0 (expected 1) and `headroom` 1 (expected 0).
- Roster 02 (`costLimit` 1999): gate closed, slot reports `effectiveMin` null, `effectiveMax` 0, `isBlocked` true — all as demanded. `00f6-...` stays silent only because its `actual` is 0 and 0 <= 0; `current` is 0 (expected 1).
- Roster 03 (`costLimit` 1999, 2000 spent): `limit::<costTypeId>` already reads the configured budget and not the spent sum — the gate stays closed, and `budget::ecfa-8486-4f6c-c249` already fires `actual` 2000 / `bound` 1999. `query.js` `resolveLimitValue` reads `ctx.budget.get(costTypeId)` from `rosterBudget.js`; nothing there needs touching. Same two gaps as roster 02.

So the acceptance criteria about `limit::`, the inclusive `atLeast`, the gated `set` and the budget rule are already met by the engine; the only missing piece is the count.

## The change

One file, `src/evaluator/constraints.js`, function `countingFlagsOf`. Widen the scope guard from ROSTER to ROSTER-or-FORCE:

```js
// before
if (limit.scope !== ScopeKeyword.ROSTER) return flags;
// after
if (limit.scope !== ScopeKeyword.ROSTER && limit.scope !== ScopeKeyword.FORCE) return flags;
```

Everything else in that function stays exactly as it is, and each guard keeps carrying its meaning for the force frame too:

- `flags?.shared === false` still returns unchanged flags: a per-instance limit is bound to its carrier's subtree, and nothing about the force frame changes that.
- `flags?.includeChildSelections === true` still returns unchanged flags: nothing to raise.
- The `counted?.kind !== DefinitionKind.ENTRY` guard still holds the raise to entry-anchored limits; group and category anchors keep their written flags.
- `includeClimbedCosts: flags?.includeChildSelections ?? false` still pins the *climbed descendant* costs to the written flag, so a force-scoped cost-type limit keeps reading only its carrier's own costs (§7.6 "just scope's field", Issue 091/0113). Only the occurrence count of the carrier itself is widened.
- `includeChildForces` is deliberately **not** raised: sub-forces stay out, per the §7.6 row quoted above.

The JSDoc block above `countingFlagsOf` (and the sentence in `resolveBound`'s block that refers to "einer geteilten, eintrags-verankerten roster-Grenze") currently names `scope="roster"` alone. Rewrite both to name roster **and** force, with the §7.6 justification and a pointer to issue 0147. Language: keep those comments **German**, matching the file and every other comment in `src/evaluator/` — the project's documentation language for this subsystem. Commit message and the backlog return stay English.

No other file changes. In particular `report.js` needs nothing: `current`, `headroom` and `isBlocked` are all derived from the max result (`report.js` lines 441-444, `current: maxResult?.actual ?? ...`, `headroom: headroomOf(maxResult)`, `isBlocked: maxResult !== null && maxResult.actual >= maxResult.bound`), so the corrected `actual` propagates by itself: roster 01 gets `current` 1 / `headroom` 0 / `isBlocked` false, rosters 02 and 03 get `current` 1 / `effectiveMax` 0 / `isBlocked` true.

## Alternatives rejected

- **Fix it in `countIndex.js`** (stop treating an intervening selection as a crossed boundary for force frames): rejected. That would silently redefine `includeChildSelections` for *every* force-scoped reader — conditions, repeats, percent denominators — not just for shared entry-anchored limits, and it would strip the engine of the distinction the flag exists for. The constraint layer is the documented place for this correction; it already owns exactly this widening for the roster frame.
- **Fix it in `report.js`** (recount the occupancy for occupied slots when the max result reads 0): rejected. It would repair `current` but leave `00f6-...` silent, so rosters 02 and 03 would still fail, and it would put a second counting site next to the query primitive, which is meant to be the only one.
- **Widen the raise to every scope** (parent, self, unit, entry-id and category-id frames): rejected as unfounded scope. For `parent`/`self` the flag's discriminating meaning is precisely nesting depth below the carrier, and no pinned scenario or catalog reading in this increment demands a change there. Only the two container frames — roster and force — carry the "all the selections of this container" reading.
- **Raise `includeChildForces` along with it**: rejected. §7.6 gives that flag its own meaning ("only from parent force selections"), and the pinned scenario has a single force, so nothing supports it.

## Measured blast radius

I applied exactly this one-line change in a throwaway `git worktree` (removed afterwards; the repository tree carries none of it) and ran the closed check command there: `npx vitest run src/evaluator` -> **83 test files, 1118 tests, all passed, exit 0**. So the change makes the three pinned cases green and regresses nothing in the evaluator's unit, scenario and cross-catalog suites as they stand at `HEAD` of this branch.

return.testPlan:
## Whether

Tests are needed. The three acceptance cases are already pinned by the untouchable E2E scenario, so they need no new test; the *rule* the fix establishes — a shared, entry-anchored limit with `scope="force"` and `includeChildSelections="false"` counts nested occurrences within its force — is not pinned anywhere by a unit test, and it must be, next to its roster twin from Issue 083.

## What

One new unit test file with five cases, all against a synthetic catalogue (no fixture catalogs).

Baseline construction shared by cases 1-4: a catalogue with one `forceEntry`, a `unit` entry "Hero" that pulls in a shared `upgrade` entry "Relic" via `entryLink`, and "Relic" carrying `<constraint type="max" value="1" field="selections" scope="force" shared="true" includeChildSelections="false" includeChildForces="false" id="..."/>`. Every Relic occurrence therefore sits one selection level below the force, exactly like the Uprising selection.

1. **Nested occurrences count within the force.** Input: one force, two Heroes, each with one Relic. Expected: the force-scoped max fires with `actual` 2 against `bound` 1. Without the fix `actual` is 0 and it stays silent.
2. **The boundary case, and the reported occupancy.** Input: one force, one Hero, one Relic. Expected: the limit does **not** fire (1 <= 1), and the capability record of the Relic slot (`defId` = the link's or the target's id as the report projects it, `anchorKind` `occupied`) reports `current` 1 — not 0. This is the exact defect the scenario's `current` 1 demands; assert `current` here, since the manifest's own assertion lives in an untouchable file.
3. **The force frame is not the roster frame.** Input: two forces of the same `forceEntry`, one Hero with one Relic in each. Expected: the max does not fire — each force counts 1, and `includeChildForces="false"` keeps the sibling force out. If the raise were mistakenly applied at roster width, or if `includeChildForces` were raised along with it, this fires with `actual` 2.
4. **`shared="false"` stays per-instance.** Same catalogue but the force-scoped `max 1` written with `shared="false"`, and two Heroes each with one Relic in one force. Expected: no violation — the count stays bound to the carrying instance (1 each). This pins the first guard of `countingFlagsOf` against the widening.
5. **Climbed descendant costs stay gated by the written flag.** Catalogue: a shared `upgrade` "Banner" with its own cost 10 in a cost type, containing a nested child selection costing 5, and "Banner" carrying `<constraint type="max" value="10" field="<costTypeId>" scope="force" shared="true" includeChildSelections="false" .../>`. One force, one Hero, one Banner with its child. Expected: no violation — `actual` is 10 (the Banner's own cost, read at any nesting depth), not 15. This pins `includeClimbedCosts` staying on the written flag when the nesting flag is raised.

**Left untested, on purpose:** the scopes `parent`, `self`, `unit`, entry-id and category-id frames — the change does not touch them, and asserting their unchanged behaviour would restate coverage the existing `constraints.*` and `query.*` tests already hold. Group- and category-anchored force-scoped limits are likewise left untested: the `DefinitionKind.ENTRY` guard that excludes them is unchanged, and the E2E scenario suite exercises them broadly. The three pinned rosters of `docs/testing/at-least-roster-points-limit` get no new test of their own — the manifest runner is their test, and the scenario directory must not be touched.

## How

All five cases are unit level, driven through the public facade `evaluate(prepareDataset({ catalogues: [xml] }), roster)` — the evaluator's only legal entry point (ADR 0030, machine-enforced by dependency-cruiser and oxlint; do not import `constraints.js` directly).

- File: `/home/user/tome_of_battle/src/evaluator/constraints.forceScopeNestedOccurrences.test.js` (new).
- Framework: Vitest.
- Command for just this file, from the repository root: `npx vitest run src/evaluator/constraints.forceScopeNestedOccurrences.test.js`.

**Suite doc:** there is no `CLAUDE.md` in `src/evaluator/` or in any test directory of this repository — the only ones are the repository-root `CLAUDE.md` and `scripts/lib/CLAUDE.md`. Do **not** write one in this increment: the increment's criteria fence the change to the engine fix and its unit test, and a new subsystem doc is neither. Take the conventions instead from the file this test is the sibling of, `src/evaluator/constraints.carrierDescendants.test.js`, which pins the identical rule for `scope="roster"`: jsdom-provided `DOMParser` at the top of the file, catalogue XML as a template literal with id constants, a local `evaluate` wrapper over the two-stage facade, roster objects as plain `{ forces: [{ defId, count, children }] }` literals, `violationsOf`/`expectFiring` helpers, and German test names. Nothing I read contradicts that file.

## What counts as done

Exactly one command, from the repository root; its exit code judges the work, and nothing else is run:

- `npx vitest run src/evaluator`

It covers the three pinned scenario cases, the new unit file, and every other evaluator unit and cross-catalog test.

## What is already red

I did not run the check list as a baseline. Red today, from the issue and confirmed by my own facade-level diagnostic: the three cases `Szenario: at-least-roster-points-limit > rosters/01-limit-2000-gate-open.ros`, `> rosters/02-limit-1999-gate-closed.ros` and `> rosters/03-limit-1999-spent-2000-gate-closed.ros`. Everything else in `src/evaluator` is expected green.

**The one run I did make, and why.** The plan turned on a question reading alone could not settle: whether widening `countingFlagsOf` from the roster frame to the force frame regresses any of the 65 pinned scenarios or the unit suite. If it did, the fix would have had to be narrower and the plan different. So I applied the one-line change in a throwaway `git worktree` outside the repository and ran `npx vitest run src/evaluator` there once: 83 test files, 1118 tests, all passed, exit 0. The worktree is removed and the repository tree carries none of that code. The new unit test file was not part of that run; it is still unwritten.
return.summary: The Uprising gate fails for one reason only: a shared, entry-anchored `max` with `scope="force"` and `includeChildSelections="false"` does not count occurrences nested below the force, so `constraints.js` reads `actual` 0 instead of 1. The fix is to widen the existing roster-frame flag raise in `countingFlagsOf` to the force frame as well — one line plus its JSDoc; measured in a throwaway worktree, it turns the whole evaluator suite green (1118 tests, exit 0). Everything else the scenario demands — the inclusive `atLeast`, the gated `set` on the constraint id, and `limit::` reading the configured budget rather than the spent sum — the engine already does correctly.
